images.title: Read a bar as about
images.purpose: Recap how to read a clustered bar graph: find the scale first, then read each bar against the guidelines as an estimate.
images.composition: One small cluster of three bars sits in the centre against a short vertical scale on the left; generous white space all round.
exact_structure: A vertical axis on the left with 5 thin grey (#6B7280) guidelines at 0, 20, 40, 60 and 80, each numbered at the left.
Exactly 1 cluster of 3 touching vertical bars: teal (#0072B2) height 30, amber (#E69F00) height 50, reddish purple (#CC79A7) height 70.
Under the cluster, small labels 2021, 2022, 2023 under the teal, amber and purple bars.
A dotted grey line runs from the top of the teal bar left to the axis, meeting it halfway between the 20 and 40 guidelines, with the label about 30 beside it.
No values printed on the bars and no other annotations.
rejection: more or fewer than 3 bars or 5 guidelines
the dotted line meeting the axis anywhere other than halfway between 20 and 40
values printed on top of bars
images.takeaway: Know the scale first, then read a bar between guidelines as an estimate.
images.description: A cluster of three bars against guidelines 0 to 80, with a dotted line showing the shortest bar is about 30.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video for this concept.
images.teaching_notes: Ask students to say the scale step out loud, then estimate the amber and purple bars the same way.

image_decisions.why: A compact recap of reading a bar between guidelines supports the practice.
